correctness.rationale: The Fourier characters are eigenvectors of U with dense eigenvalues on the circle. For a≠b, conjugation of diag(aU,bU) by the upper shear S with off-diagonal M_h gives coupling b h−a h∘R_α=c. The Fourier denominator b−a exp(inα) is nonzero and the finite sum defines a bounded multiplier; this fixes the sign of the conjugated Riesz projection, whose row is (1,−h) pointwise and whose norm is sqrt(1+||h||∞²). The known ergodic component bound for a two-dimensional fiber applies; this operator attains it. Near a=b=r the nonzero-frequency part of h converges uniformly, while the constant term is exactly c_0/(b−a). Its norm differs from that term's modulus by a bounded amount even for either sign of b−a. This proves the scaled gap limit and the bounded norm limit for c_0=0. The two-mode norm follows by exact phase alignment, including when either coefficient vanishes. At collision, write c=c_0+r(h−h∘R_α) using the nonzero harmonics. Directly raising the triangular factorization to the N-th power and removing diag(U^N,U^N) leaves unit diagonal and off-diagonal multiplication by Nc_0/r+h−h∘R_α^N. The last two terms are uniformly bounded; the diagonal contributes norm one, so dividing by N yields |c_0|/r and the power-boundedness criterion for r^(−N)T^N. Off the circle the triangular resolvent is invertible, and the invariant first-coordinate subspace supplies the dense eigenvalues on the circle, so no further spectral issue arises at collision. The proof's 'rank-one upper-block' terminology refers to fiber rank, not rank on the whole L² space; only its norm is used.
residual_risks: Frozen replay path is python3 check.py. Its 4380 recorded finite assertions sample the cohomological relation and phase maximum; they are not a power-growth or arbitrary-angle certificate. Code was inspected, not independently executed.
The collided limit idempotent for c_0=0 is not a Riesz splitting of the single coincident circle.

value.rationale: The known component bound addresses how many spectral pieces can occur, not whether the splitting stays well conditioned as two pieces meet. This exact two-fiber model is a useful benchmark: the same scalar harmonic controls sharp reciprocal-gap conditioning and quantitative amplification after collision, while a mean-zero near-resonant harmonic shows a different, large but finite conditioning scale at fixed angle. The general norm identity plus explicit two-frequency evaluation make these regimes distinguishable without spectral discretization.
residual_risks: No uniform control over all irrational angles or arbitrary infinite Fourier couplings is asserted; small divisors can invalidate the bounded collision shear outside the frozen class.
